scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Make the read routes check a bearer token or a shared secret from a flag or env var in the collector itself, or bind a second listener for the report route only so that the public listener carries nothing else. Refuse to start with a non-loopback --listen unless an auth option is set. Add a test asserting that GET routes need a credential.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Demonstrated in the source: no check exists in the router. Whether it is exposed depends on the deployment, which the source does not show. Confirm on the master host that oauth2-proxy or nginx covers every path except POST /v1/report.

scanner_findings.title: The certificate endpoint check compares the certificate with itself, so no endpoint binding is applied to reports
scanner_findings.prerequisites: A holder of a valid membership certificate issued by the registry key for network 'net', covering identity X, but with an endpoint ID of some other node or of none in particular. The attacker also holds the secret key of identity X, so the report signature is valid.
scanner_findings.impact: The endpoint named in the certificate is read from the certificate and then used for the check. The check therefore cannot fail for endpoint reasons. A report is accepted for any covered identity whichever endpoint the certificate names, so the cert-to-node binding that peers rely on in the handshake is not applied to telemetry. Impact is limited because a covered identity key is still required.
scanner_findings.evidence: 'let endpoint = EndpointId::from_bytes(&cert.payload().endpoint_id)' followed by 'policy.check_cert(&cert, endpoint, now)?;'. The endpoint passed in is taken from the same cert, so the value being compared is not independent of the certificate.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Do not derive the expected endpoint from the certificate. Require the endpoint from the report (or the node's known endpoint from the registry or the store) and pass that to check_cert, or document that telemetry deliberately ignores endpoint binding and state it in the telemetry module docs. Add a test where the cert endpoint differs from the expected one.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Code reading shows the check is circular here. Whether check_cert also enforces an endpoint binding elsewhere is not visible in the supplied files (record.rs and membership.rs are missing), so confirm there before acting on it.

scanner_findings.title: Rate limit is keyed per signing identity, so one member with several covered identities gets several bursts
scanner_findings.prerequisites: A member holds a membership certificate covering several identities (the certificate lists identities, and the record module allows up to 16 per record). The member holds the keys of those identities.
scanner_findings.impact: Each identity has its own token bucket and its own entry in the node map and metrics, so one member can send about 3 reports per identity burst and then one every min_interval per identity. This defeats the per-node limit that the docs promise and can fill MAX_NODES with that member's identities. This is member-only abuse, but it crosses the identity boundary the limit is meant to enforce.
scanner_findings.evidence: 'let mut bucket = prev.and_then(|p| p.bucket).unwrap_or(Bucket { tokens: RATE_BURST, at_ms: now, });' where prev is self.nodes.get(&id) and id is the signing identity. The docs say 'per node at most one report per --min-report-interval on average'.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Key the bucket by the member (the certificate's endpoint ID, or a canonical identity of the cert) rather than the signing identity, and count all of a certificate's identities against one bucket. Alternatively cap the number of identities per certificate that the collector accepts for reporting.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Code reading shows the keying. Confirm with a test that one certificate covering two identities gets two buckets. Whether a real network issues multi-identity certificates is not visible from the supplied files.

scanner_findings.title: Telemetry digest has no network binding: a report signed for one closed network can be replayed to another network's collector
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The same node identity must be a member of two closed networks that use different registries and different collector URLs. The attacker must obtain a signed report of that node from network A and deliver it to network B's collector within the collector's 5 min clock-skew window, and that report's timestamp must be newer than B's last accepted timestamp for the node. Delivery could be done by a malicious collector or relay of network A.
scanner_findings.impact: Network B's collector accepts a report that its members never sent to it. The attacker can inject fake counters, fake connection lists, or a stopping=true report that marks the node offline in B's dashboard and metrics until its next genuine report. The attacker cannot forge a signature, so this is limited to replaying reports the identity really signed.
scanner_findings.evidence: telemetry.rs:34 `pub const DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"golem-p2p/telemetry/v1\0";` and telemetry.rs:46-51 `pub fn digest(body: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] { let mut h = Sha256::new(); h.update(DOMAIN); h.update(body); h.finalize().into() }`. The network name is not in the digest, and verify (telemetry.rs:96-118) checks the network only through the certificate, which is not covered by the signature. collector.rs:471-477 passes the network-independent digest to `golem_p2p::telemetry::verify(&self.config.policy, body, &sig, &cert, ...)`.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Include the network name in the signed digest, for example h.update(DOMAIN); h.update(&(network.len() as u64).to_be_bytes()); h.update(network.as_bytes()); h.update(body), with the network taken from the policy in both sign and verify. Add a test that a report signed for network A fails verification under network B's policy.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Write a test with one identity that holds valid certificates for two networks with different registry keys. Sign a report for network A's digest, then call verify with network B's policy and a valid B certificate. Confirm it is accepted, which demonstrates the defect. Also check that the record and membership signature domains differ from b"golem-p2p/telemetry/v1\0", since the source for those is not supplied.

scanner_findings.title: Unbounded interval_s makes status() overflow under the collector lock
scanner_findings.prerequisites: An attacker holding a valid membership certificate (an insider or a compromised member) signs a report with interval_s around 1e16 or more. validate() only checks is_finite, so the report is accepted and stored in nodes.
scanner_findings.impact: Under debug or overflow-checks builds, 3 * interval overflows and panics inside status(), which runs under the shared Mutex in state(), metrics(), tick() and merged_links(). The mutex is poisoned and every later lock().expect(poisoned) panics, so the collector stops serving until restart. In release builds the arithmetic wraps, so the node is misclassified as online, stale or offline for no valid reason.
scanner_findings.evidence: let interval = (n.report.interval_s.max(1.0) * 1000.0) as u64; ... if age <= 3 * interval + 2000 { "online" } else if age <= (6 * interval).max(60_000) { "stale" }. Also validate(): if !r.interval_s.is_finite() || !r.delta_s.is_finite() { return Err("invalid number") } with no upper bound.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Reject interval_s and delta_s above a sane maximum (for example 3600 s) in validate(), and use saturating_mul and saturating_add in status(). Add a test that sends interval_s of 1e16 and checks that the collector stays responsive.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Demonstrated by reading the code. Run a debug-build test that accepts such a report and then calls state(); confirm the panic and the later poisoned-lock panics.

scanner_findings.title: Attacker-chosen path_s overflows when converted to milliseconds under the lock
scanner_findings.prerequisites: A member sends a report whose connection has path_s greater than about 1.8e16 (u64::MAX / 1000). validate() does not check path_s, and the report's peer and relay fields are otherwise valid.
scanner_findings.impact: In debug or overflow-checks builds, s * 1000 panics inside merged_links(), which runs under the shared Mutex in state(), metrics() and tick(). This poisons the mutex and takes down the collector, as in the previous finding.
scanner_findings.evidence: path_since: latest.c.path_s.map(|s| latest.ts.saturating_sub(s * 1000)),  where path_s is Option<u64> in Conn and is deserialized directly from the signed report body.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Use s.saturating_mul(1000) here, or cap path_s in validate() to the report's own interval and to the retention window. Add a test with path_s set to u64::MAX.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis that needs a test: in a debug or test build, post such a report and then call state(); expect an arithmetic overflow panic.

scanner_findings.title: Counter sums overflow with attacker-chosen delta values under the lock
scanner_findings.prerequisites: A member sends reports whose delta counters (conns_new, requests_ok and similar) are near u64::MAX. Two such reports in one sampling window, or a report added to already-large pending totals, are enough. validate() does not check counter magnitudes.
scanner_findings.impact: In debug or overflow-checks builds, the += in Counts::add panics inside accept(), which holds the shared Mutex. The lock is poisoned and the collector stops serving. Later sums (aggregate, state's hour sum) can overflow the same way. In release builds the sums silently wrap and the dashboard totals become wrong.
scanner_findings.evidence: fn add(&mut self, o: &Counts) { self.conns_new += o.conns_new; self.conns_failed += o.conns_failed; ... } called from accept_inner with counts built from report.delta.conns_new and similar fields, all deserialized from the body.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Use saturating_add in Counts::add and in aggregate() and state(). Optionally cap per-report delta counters in validate() against the report's interval.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Demonstrated by reading the code. A unit test that accepts two reports with conns_new of u64::MAX - 1 and then calls tick() would show the panic in debug builds.

scanner_findings.title: A single panic under the shared Mutex takes the whole collector down and silently stops sampling
scanner_findings.prerequisites: Any panic while the collector Mutex is held, such as the overflows in the earlier findings or any future unwrap in Collector methods. No attacker action is needed beyond the first panic.
scanner_findings.impact: The Mutex is poisoned. Every subsequent expect(poisoned) fails in tick_loop (line 1352), report (1397), state (1423), nodes (1428), history (1448), metrics (1463) and shutdown (141). The sampler task is spawned and never joined, so its panic is only logged by tokio and sampling stops silently while the HTTP server keeps answering 500s or closing connections. Recovery requires a restart.
scanner_findings.evidence: async fn tick_loop(shared: Shared) { loop { ... shared.lock().expect("poisoned").tick(now_ms()); } } and async fn report(...) { let r = s.lock().expect("poisoned").accept(&body, &headers, now_ms()); ... }
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Recover from poisoning with lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) in every handler and in tick_loop, or use parking_lot::Mutex, which does not poison. Also log and restart the sampler if its task ends. Keep the panic surface small by fixing the overflows above.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Demonstrated by reading the code. A test that poisons the mutex (for example by panicking inside accept under a test hook) and then calls the report route would show that later requests fail.

scanner_findings.title: Blocking file writes and a full state dump run while the request lock is held
scanner_findings.prerequisites: A minute boundary is crossed (push_minute, every 60 ticks), or the hourly fine-file rewrite runs. Many nodes are stored (up to MAX_NODES, which is 10000). Report and dashboard requests are arriving at the same time.
scanner_findings.impact: push_minute calls save_nodes, which serializes every stored NodeState and writes nodes.json synchronously. push_fine rewrites fine.jsonl synchronously. Both run inside tick() under the std Mutex. Report and dashboard handlers wait for the lock and block a Tokio worker thread while they wait. Under load this adds latency spikes that can cause the 5 s reporting timeout to fire on members.
scanner_findings.evidence: fn push_minute(&mut self, m: Sample, now: u64) { ... self.save_nodes(); } and fn save_nodes(&self) { let text = serde_json::to_string(&self.nodes).expect("encode nodes"); ... write_atomic(&dir.join("nodes.json"), ...) }, while tick_loop calls shared.lock().expect("poisoned").tick(now_ms()) on the async runtime.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot the data under the lock and do the file writes on a blocking thread (tokio::task::spawn_blocking) or on a dedicated writer task fed by a channel. Use tokio::sync::Mutex or a message-passing design so that no synchronous I/O runs under the lock on the async runtime.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis that needs a load test: measure report latency during a minute boundary with thousands of stored nodes.

scanner_findings.title: Telemetry URL with embedded credentials written to logs and JSON events
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The operator sets --telemetry or GOLEM_P2P_TELEMETRY to a URL with userinfo (https://user:pass@collector/), or the registry advertises such a URL, on a closed network.
scanner_findings.impact: The password is written to the log at info level and to the JSON event stream, where it is visible to anyone who can read logs or events. The same URL is repeated in the warn line on failure.
scanner_findings.evidence: Line 594: info!("telemetry: reporting to {u} (opt out: --no-telemetry)"); lines 604-613: out.event("telemetry").field("url", match &target { Some(Target::Fixed(u)) => Some(u.to_string()), ... }); line 750: warn!("telemetry: report to {url} failed: ..."). url::Url::to_string keeps userinfo.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Log and emit only scheme, host and path (strip username and password, query and fragment) with a small helper, and reject userinfo in --telemetry at parse time, pointing users to a header or proxy instead.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Unit test that a URL with credentials produces log and event output without the password. Demonstrated code defect: the string is formatted as-is.

scanner_findings.title: Store files written with default permissions expose network topology to other local users
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The collector runs on a shared host with a permissive umask, and another local user can read the --store directory.
scanner_findings.impact: nodes.json, minutes-*.jsonl and fine.jsonl hold node IDs, names, versions, relay URLs, the connection graph, NAT summaries and last error kinds. Local users can read this, and nodes.json also keeps full reports.
scanner_findings.evidence: write_atomic: std::fs::write(&tmp, data)? then rename; append() uses std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).open(&path) with no mode; the store directory is created with std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir) at line 394. No set_permissions or mode(0o600) appears.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Create the store directory with mode 0700 and each file with mode 0600 (std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt / DirBuilderExt), or document that the store must sit in a private directory.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Check the resulting file modes under a typical umask. Hypothesis: whether this matters depends on the host's sharing and the sensitivity the operator assigns to topology.

scanner_findings.title: Collector router serves full state, history and metrics with no authentication in code
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The listener is reachable and the proxy in front does not restrict every route to authenticated users, for example if only POST /v1/report is configured.
scanner_findings.impact: Anyone who reaches the collector can read every node's name, version, commit, OS, NAT booleans, home relay, connections (peer IDs and relay URLs), totals and last error kind through /v1/state, /v1/nodes, /v1/history and /metrics. This is more than the members' network needs to see, and it matches the lens's concern about detail given to remote parties.
scanner_findings.evidence: router() registers "/v1/state", "/v1/nodes", "/v1/history", "/metrics" and "/" with no auth layer; the module doc says the other routes must be protected by the proxy (nginx basic auth on master). Node JSON in state() includes "nat", "commit", "last_error" and "home_relay".
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Enforce authentication in the service (a shared bearer token or header check on non-report routes) and fail closed when not configured, instead of relying only on deployment documentation. Alternatively, bind the non-report routes to a separate listener.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis: depends on deployment. Confirm the proxy configuration on master and whether the collector listens on a public address by default (default is 127.0.0.1:8091).

scanner_findings.title: Remote error body logged unescaped at warn level
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The configured collector or registry answers reports with a body containing control characters or terminal escape sequences, for example a hostile or compromised collector, or a MITM on plain HTTP.
scanner_findings.impact: The first 200 characters of the response body are printed to the operator's terminal or log through the warn line, so forged lines or escape sequences can reach it. The body is only truncated by chars, not stripped of control characters.
scanner_findings.evidence: Line 705: text.chars().take(200).collect::<String>(); the Display impl at line 666 formats through golem_p2p::membership::error_text(*s, body); the warn at lines 749-751 interpolates {e}. The control-character filtering inside error_text is not visible in the supplied files.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Strip or escape control characters from the body before logging (for example, keep only printable ASCII), or log only the status code and a fixed reason string.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis: check whether golem_p2p::membership::error_text already removes control characters; the file is not supplied. The directory is plain HTTP by design, so an on-path attacker can reach this path.

scanner_findings.title: Download status parser panics on a non-char-boundary slice of listener-controlled text
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The user runs probe --bulk-related download, or bench/soak download, against a node that is malicious or replaced by an impostor that answers the download request. The listener sends a first line that does not start with 'ok bytes=' and contains no newline, e.g. 'a' followed by 150 two-byte UTF-8 characters, then closes the stream. Nothing else is required.
scanner_findings.impact: The client process panics and aborts mid-run, losing the rest of the measurement and its JSON summary. A single hostile reply from a listener is enough to crash the CLI.
scanner_findings.evidence: read_status_line returns the whole buffer lossy-decoded when it is longer than 256 bytes or the stream ends without a newline (lines 851-859). In download, the status is checked with strip_prefix (line 784), and on failure the error context slices with: &status[..status.len().min(100)] (line 789). The slice index is a byte index on a String, so it panics when byte 100 falls inside a multi-byte character. 'a' followed by 'é' repeated 150 times puts byte 100 in the middle of a character.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Truncate by characters, not bytes, for the message, e.g. status.chars().take(100).collect::<String>(), or truncate at a char boundary with floor_char_boundary-style logic. Also cap the status buffer during reading: check buf.len() before extending it with the whole chunk rather than after, and return an error when no newline appears within 256 bytes.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Demonstrated code defect by inspection. Confirm with a unit test that calls the error path of download with a 301-byte status of the form 'a' followed by 150 'é' and no newline, using a mock RecvStream or a loopback listener that writes that and finishes.

scanner_findings.title: Download reads without a deadline and never enforces the announced size while reading
scanner_findings.prerequisites: download is called with max_time None, which the code allows (the deadline is optional), and the listener is malicious. It announces a small 'ok bytes=N' and then keeps sending data, or sends it slowly, without ever finishing the stream. Whether any caller passes None is not visible in the supplied files (bench and soak are not supplied).
scanner_findings.impact: The download loop reads until the stream ends with no bound on time or bytes. got is only compared with announced after the loop (line 828), so the excess is consumed and counted, not refused. A listener can hold the client's task and its bandwidth indefinitely, and the bench or soak run never finishes.
scanner_findings.evidence: With no deadline, the loop is: None => recv.read_chunk(usize::MAX).await, and it breaks only on Ok(None) or a read error (lines 807-823). The size check comes only afterwards: if !by_time && got != announced { bail!(...) } (lines 828-830). Nothing stops reading once got exceeds announced. Also, read_status_line is awaited with no timeout when max_time is None (line 778).
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Stop reading once got reaches announced (read exactly announced bytes, and treat anything beyond as a protocol error). Apply a default timeout to the status read and to the body read, or make max_time mandatory for download. Bound the total time by the transfer timeout passed in from the callers.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis until the callers are checked: confirm whether any call site passes max_time None. If one does, a test with a listener that sends more than announced bytes and then stalls should show the loop running past the expected end. Demonstrated for the code shown.

scanner_findings.title: Download status error path slices remote text at a fixed byte offset and can panic
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The client runs download() (probe --bulk does not download, but bench and soak do) against a malicious listen node that replies with a status line that does not start with 'ok bytes=' and is not a 'refused' reply. read_status_line returns up to about 256 bytes or more if no newline appears, so the status can be longer than 100 bytes. Byte 100 must fall inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character, which the attacker controls (for example 99 ASCII bytes followed by a 2-byte character).
scanner_findings.impact: Panic in the client task that aborts the whole CLI command (tokio::main unwinds to process exit 101). A malicious listener can crash probe, bench or soak at will. The error path is reached only when the announced size is wrong, so it is a demonstrated code defect reachable from remote bytes, not a hypothetical.
scanner_findings.evidence: let announced: u64 = status.strip_prefix("ok bytes=").and_then(|n| n.trim().parse().ok()).with_context(|| { format!("listener does not support downloads (an older golem-p2p?): {}", &status[..status.len().min(100)]) })?; with status built by String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf) in read_status_line, which allows buf.len() > 256 before breaking.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Truncate on a char boundary, for example with status.chars().take(100).collect::<String>() or by truncating the bytes before from_utf8_lossy. Add a unit test with a multi-byte character straddling byte 100.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Demonstrated code defect by reading. Confirm with a unit test that calls the status parsing with a 100-byte-straddling UTF-8 string, or with a fake listener that sends such a line.

scanner_findings.title: Blocking stdout write while holding a std mutex inside async tasks
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The stdout consumer of --json output stops reading (pipe full, controller hung). Events are emitted from async tasks (observer tasks, pinger, telemetry) on tokio worker threads.
scanner_findings.impact: Each emit blocks a runtime worker thread inside writeln! while the sealed std::sync::Mutex is held, so other emitters block on the lock as well. Enough stalled workers can freeze connection handling and the request path. This is a hypothesis that needs a test with a non-reading stdout pipe; it is not demonstrated.
scanner_findings.evidence: fn write(&self, line: &str, last: bool) { let mut sealed = self.inner.sealed.lock().expect("poisoned"); if *sealed { return; } let mut stdout = std::io::stdout().lock(); let _ = writeln!(stdout, "{line}"); let _ = stdout.flush(); *sealed = last; }
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Send events over a bounded channel to one dedicated writer thread, or use spawn_blocking for the write, and drop or count events when the channel is full instead of blocking the caller.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis: run a probe --json with stdout piped to a process that stops reading, and check whether the runtime stalls. The sealed lock also needs a check for lock poisoning, which is unlikely since nothing panics while holding it.

scanner_findings.title: Huge user-supplied durations overflow Instant arithmetic and panic
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The operator passes a very large --duration or --timeout (parse::duration accepts any value that Duration::try_from_secs_f64 accepts, up to about 1.8e19 seconds). This is local operator input, not remote input.
scanner_findings.impact: tokio Instant addition panics on overflow, so probe aborts at startup with a panic instead of a clean argument error. Exit code and message are unhelpful, but the impact is limited to the local operator. The same pattern appears in end + timeout on line 193 and in upload() start + t, which are not reached remotely.
scanner_findings.evidence: let end = tokio::time::Instant::now() + duration; // A request in flight at the end may take up to one more timeout. let hard_end = end + timeout;
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Use checked_add in parse::duration or at the call sites, and return a clap error when the deadline cannot be represented; cap the accepted range to something like a few days.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Demonstrated by arithmetic reasoning: run probe with --duration 18446744073709551615 and confirm the panic. Low practical risk, since the input comes from the operator.

scanner_findings.title: Remote listener reply printed raw to the terminal in send
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The operator runs 'golem-p2p send' without --json against a node that an attacker controls, or that a malicious listener answers. The attacker controls the bytes of the echo reply.
scanner_findings.impact: The reply goes to stdout unchanged. A reply with newlines can forge additional output lines, and one with ANSI or OSC escape sequences can rewrite or hide earlier terminal output. Output piped into scripts can be spoofed the same way. JSON mode is not affected because serde escapes the text.
scanner_findings.evidence: println!("{} ({} ms, {})", String::from_utf8_lossy(&reply), r.rtt.as_millis(), path_name(r.path)); where reply is the Ok(reply) value returned by pinger.ping, i.e. the peer's bytes.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Escape control characters before printing peer-supplied text in human mode, for example by replacing every char that is control (including ESC and newline) with a visible escape such as \u{..}, or by printing hex when the reply is not printable ASCII. Apply the same helper to every human-mode print of peer text (see the probe.rs finding).
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Demonstrated by reading the code: a test listener that replies with a string containing a newline and ESC[2J should show the raw bytes on stdout. Confirm with a small harness run.

scanner_findings.title: Remote error and refusal text printed raw in probe and bench human output
scanner_findings.prerequisites: A malicious listener returns an unexpected reply, a refused reply with arbitrary detail text, or a status line that fails parsing. The operator runs probe or bench without --json.
scanner_findings.impact: The peer-controlled text (up to 200 bytes of an unexpected reply, up to 4096 bytes of a refusal, or up to 256 bytes of a download status line) is embedded in errors and printed with println! and eprintln!. This allows the same forged-line and terminal-escape injection as in the send finding. The main.rs 'Error: {e:?}' path also prints the error chain.
scanner_findings.evidence: Err(e) => println!("bulk {} bytes failed: {e:#}", b.bytes), where e may come from Refused::parse(&reply) with reply built from the peer's bytes; probe.rs line 96 builds the message from String::from_utf8_lossy(&r[..r.len().min(200)]), and main.rs line 767 prints it with println!("seq={} failed after {} ms: {e:#}", ...).
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Sanitize at the source: when building 'unexpected reply' and Refused details from peer bytes, map control characters to escapes before they enter an error. That covers human output and anyhow chains, and the JSON path already escapes them.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis that needs a test: a listener that answers 'refused reason=x\u001b[2J' or a newline-bearing string should produce unescaped terminal output in the human path. Verify by running the probe against a stub listener.

scanner_findings.title: Echo reply from a malicious listener is buffered without a size check before the byte comparison
scanner_findings.prerequisites: A malicious peer that the operator benchmarks with `bench --to`, and whose reply to an echo request is larger than the request. The golem-p2p request path must not cap reply size, which this file does not show.
scanner_findings.impact: If `ep.request` does not cap the reply, a malicious listener can make the client allocate its whole reply in memory before the `ends_with` check. Concurrency runs up to 64 streams, so the allocation multiplies by the stream count.
scanner_findings.evidence: let reply = ep.request(to, &payload).await?; if !reply.ends_with(&payload) { bail!("unexpected reply"); }
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the reply cap in golem-p2p's request implementation. If it is absent or larger than the request size, cap replies at the request size plus a small margin. Compare the length first and reject oversized replies before buffering.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis, not demonstrated. Run a test listener that answers a 64-byte request with a 1 GiB reply and measure the client's peak RSS. The same test applies to the soak requester at soak.rs:348.

scanner_findings.title: Lookup-time map keyed by peer id grows with every lookup and is never pruned
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The endpoint calls `Discovery::lookup` for node IDs that the peer chooses, for example identities taken from incoming connections or relay-compare traffic. The source given here does not show that path.
scanner_findings.impact: The map gains one entry per distinct node ID looked up. Those IDs can be attacker-chosen, so a peer that causes many lookups makes the map grow without bound for the life of the bench run. The run is short, so the impact is limited.
scanner_findings.evidence: self.lookups.lock().expect("poisoned").insert(id, start.elapsed());
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Store only the lookup time for the `to` node and the relay-compare node, or cap the map size and evict. Alternatively keep only the most recent lookup for `to`.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis. Check whether golem-p2p calls Discovery::lookup for inbound or attacker-supplied IDs. If it does, count map entries after a run in which a peer triggers many such lookups.

scanner_findings.title: FILT requests amplify into several datagrams, including attacker-chosen ports of a spoofed source
scanner_findings.prerequisites: Any sender that can reach a reflector UDP port and can spoof the source address (no handshake on UDP). The reflector must have more than one UDP socket, or the request must include extra ports.
scanner_findings.impact: One FILT datagram of about 20 bytes produces one MAPPED reply, up to (number of sockets - 1) UNSOL packets, and up to max_extra_ports (default 4) TOPORT packets. The TOPORT packets go to the spoofed source IP on ports the request chooses, so the reflector can be used to send unsolicited UDP traffic to third parties. The docstring promises only that each reply is small, which does not cover the number of replies.
scanner_findings.evidence: Line 114: for p in parts[2 : 2 + args.max_extra_ports]: ... Line 123: heapq.heappush(pending, (when, seq, sock, msg.encode(), (src[0], port))). Lines 108-113 push one UNSOL per other UDP socket to src. Line 23 says replies are no larger than the request plus a few dozen bytes, but says nothing about the count. Demonstrated code defect: the fan-out and the arbitrary destination port are in the code. Reflection against a real victim needs a test.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Do not send unsolicited packets to a source port the client merely asserts. Either drop the TOPORT feature or send TOPORT probes only after the client proves it owns the address, for example by echoing a value the reflector sent to that address. Cap FILT fan-out per source and per time window, and document the multiplication factor.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Send spoofed FILT datagrams from a test host with a second host as the victim and count the bytes and packets the victim receives per request. Confirm the port selection is attacker-controlled.

scanner_findings.title: Pending send queue has no bound
scanner_findings.prerequisites: A high rate of FILT datagrams, which may use spoofed or many source addresses. The delay (default 0.2 s) keeps entries queued.
scanner_findings.impact: Each FILT adds (sockets - 1) + up to 4 heap entries, each holding a copy of the payload, and nothing caps the heap size. Memory grows with request rate times delay times fan-out. This is bounded by the send rate rather than unbounded, but it is an easy way to make the reflector consume memory.
scanner_findings.evidence: Line 71: pending = []  # heap of (when, seq, sock, payload, dest). Lines 113 and 123 push without any length check. Lines 124-130 drain only entries whose time has come.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Cap len(pending) and drop FILT requests when the cap is reached. Add a per-source FILT rate limit before the fan-out is queued.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis: flood FILT at the maximum rate the host can receive and measure the heap size and RSS over a minute.

scanner_findings.title: natcheck crashes on a malformed MAPPED reply
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The reflector named by --map returns a MAPPED reply whose third field is not ip:port, which requires a malicious or broken reflector, or an on-path attacker who knows the nonce. The nonce is 48 random bits, so an off-path attacker is unlikely to match it.
scanner_findings.impact: The client stops with an uncaught ValueError from parse_addr instead of reporting the mapping. This is a robustness issue in a diagnostic client, not a remote compromise.
scanner_findings.evidence: Line 56: if len(parts) >= 3 and parts[0] == 'MAPPED' and parts[1] == nonce: return parts[2], nonce. Line 98: preserved = bool(got) and all(parse_addr(o)[1] == lport for o in got). parse_addr (line 35) calls rsplit(':', 1) and unpacks two values, so a token without a colon raises ValueError.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Validate parts[2] with a try/except around parse_addr in query or mapping_test, and treat an invalid reply as no reply.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Run the mapping test against a local fake reflector that returns MAPPED x VIA y and confirm the traceback.

scanner_findings.title: Command output and git archive are read without size limits or timeouts in the tool runner
scanner_findings.prerequisites: A repository whose tracked content makes a tool emit very large output, for example a large PR under scan, or a slow git archive or tar step.
scanner_findings.impact: Subprocess output is held in memory in full, and the git archive and tar calls have no timeout, so a very large or stuck step can exhaust memory or hang the run. The tools are run by the operator on HEAD, so this is a hypothesis about operational robustness rather than a remote attack.
scanner_findings.evidence: Line 66-67: subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, env=self.env, capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace', timeout=timeout). Lines 266-268: subprocess.run(['git', 'archive', '--format=tar', 'HEAD'], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout and subprocess.run(['tar', '-x', ...], input=archive, check=True) with no timeout.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Cap the captured output size, and give git archive and tar the same timeout the runner uses. Stream the archive to a file instead of holding it in memory.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis: run the gitleaks step against a repository with a multi-gigabyte tracked file and observe memory and time.

scanner_findings.title: Anthropic API key is inherited by every deterministic tool subprocess
scanner_findings.prerequisites: The operator exports ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment before running harness/security_graph.py (the non-interactive path). A tool then runs in the working tree, for example cargo clippy or cargo audit, which compiles and runs build.rs scripts of workspace crates and dependencies, or semgrep runs rules. The working tree may hold uncommitted changes, since run_tools reads ROOT and not the --source-ref commit.
scanner_findings.impact: Any code executed by a deterministic tool can read the API key from its environment and send it elsewhere. The key is also present in the environment of every child process, although the interactive getpass path avoids this.
scanner_findings.evidence: self.env = dict(os.environ, PATH=f"{tools_dir}:{os.environ.get('PATH', '')}", CARGO_TERM_COLOR="never", NO_COLOR="1") and then subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, env=self.env, ...) in Runner.run at line 66. api_key() in security_graph.py reads the same variable only after the tools have already run.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Build the tool environment from an explicit allowlist (PATH, HOME, CARGO_HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, locale) and remove ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and other *_KEY, *_TOKEN variables. Pass the key only to the AsyncAnthropic constructor.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Export a sentinel ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, add a build.rs under a temporary workspace crate that writes the variable to a file, run security_tools with --only clippy-panics, and check whether the sentinel appears. This is a hypothesis until that test is run.

scanner_findings.title: Working-tree file names, including untracked files, are written into the run report
scanner_findings.prerequisites: Untracked local files exist in the working tree at scan time, such as key files, .env files or local notes. The report is written to the run directory and is not redacted.
scanner_findings.impact: The names of untracked files are published in plan.json and summary.json. This can reveal the existence of secret material, which is minor in practice but is an unnecessary disclosure.
scanner_findings.evidence: "git_status": single.git("status", "--porcelain").splitlines(), inside the metadata dict that is written to plan.json at line 537 and merged into summary.json.
scanner_findings.suggested_fix: Record only the count of modified and untracked entries, or restrict the status to tracked paths (git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no), and drop path names from the artifact.
scanner_findings.validation_needed: Create an untracked file with a distinctive name, run harness/security_graph.py --dry-run, and check whether the name appears in plan.json. This is a demonstrated behaviour but its impact depends on where the run directory is stored.

summary.overview: 74 scanner findings merged into 49 candidates, with 13 IDs sent to noise. The core library shows no remotely triggerable panic. The strongest remote issues are resource-bound gaps. (1) The node connection table can be filled by cheap valid handshakes that then idle (endpoint.rs:1100). (2) The telemetry collector takes all of its work under one std Mutex, and member-controlled numbers and link keys are not bounded. That allows unbounded link history, overflow panics that poison the lock (build-dependent) and signature work under the lock. (3) The bench/soak download path panics when it slices remote status text on a byte boundary (probe.rs:789). (4) The lab UDP reflector fans out to spoofed sources on attacker-chosen ports. Several local or operator issues are confirmed in code: the tmp-file mode on the registry state file, an early transfer-slot release, a request-time budget reset, a circular endpoint check in telemetry verify, and unescaped remote text reaching the terminal. Known limits were filtered out. records/crypto#2 and closed-network/dos#3 are kept as known_limit and say what is new.

candidates.title: Inbound connection table (max_connections) can be filled by cheap valid handshakes that then stay idle; no per-source or per-identity cap
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows the only established-connection bound is the global check at 1100. Records cost nothing to make (known limit), so in an open network one process can complete up to 1024 Hellos with self-signed records. If it keeps the connections alive with QUIC PINGs, honest inbound dials are refused. The known limit only covers the 128 pre-Hello slots for 10 s; post-handshake occupancy is new. It depends on the iroh/quinn idle timeout and keep-alive, which are not shown. In closed networks it needs a member certificate.
candidates.impact: One anonymous host blocks all inbound connections to a node for as long as it likes.
candidates.suggested_fix: Add a per-source-IP and per-identity cap on established connections. Reserve capacity for known or outbound peers. Close connections with no application or control activity after a bounded time.
candidates.disagreement: The scanner rated it medium. It is raised here because it is a remote DoS on any node in an open network.

candidates.title: Download status error path byte-slices peer-controlled String at index 100 and panics on a non-char boundary
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows &status[..status.len().min(100)] on a lossily decoded peer status line. A multi-byte char straddling byte 100 panics. This path is reached whenever the status does not start with 'ok bytes='.
candidates.impact: A malicious or impostor listener crashes bench/soak download runs (the CLI process or its task).
candidates.suggested_fix: Truncate by chars (status.chars().take(100)). Also cap read_status_line before extending the buffer.
candidates.disagreement: Both scanners rated it high. It is lowered to medium because the impact is a crash of an operator-run measurement client, not of a node, directory, registry or collector.

candidates.title: Collector stores every reported link with invented peer IDs for the full retention window (unbounded history growth by one member)
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt at 693-707 inserts every link into each sample with no cap on distinct keys. The reviewer cites validate() parsing peer as NodeId only. One member can add 256 new keys per report every ~4 s, and they are kept for 7 days.
candidates.impact: Collector memory and disk grow linearly with time, driven by one certificate holder. Every history query and minute aggregation slows down.
candidates.suggested_fix: Keep links only when both ends are known reporting nodes. Cap link keys per sample and per minute, and count overflow.

candidates.title: Lab UDP reflector: one FILT datagram fans out to several datagrams, including attacker-chosen ports of a spoofed source; pending heap unbounded
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows one UNSOL per other socket sent to src, plus up to max_extra_ports TOPORT packets to (src[0], port) with a request-chosen port. UDP src is spoofable, and heappush has no length check.
candidates.impact: An internet-reachable reflector can be used to send unsolicited UDP to third parties (packet-count amplification). A FILT flood also grows memory.
candidates.suggested_fix: Require proof of address ownership before sending TOPORT and UNSOL. Rate-limit FILT per source. Cap len(pending).
candidates.disagreement: harness-python/dos#1 rated it high. It is rated medium here because this is a lab tool with a small byte amplification factor.

candidates.title: Single panic under the collector Mutex poisons it; all handlers and the detached sampler then fail until restart
candidates.reasoning: The excerpts show lock().expect("poisoned") in tick_loop and report. tick_loop is spawned and never restarted. This amplifies any panic under the lock, including the overflow candidate below.
candidates.impact: Turns any reachable panic into a permanent collector outage. Sampling stops silently.
candidates.suggested_fix: Use lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) or parking_lot. Supervise tick_loop.

candidates.title: Member-signed numeric fields (interval_s, path_s, delta counters) overflow in arithmetic under the collector lock
candidates.reasoning: The excerpts confirm the overflows. (f64*1000) as u64 saturates to u64::MAX and then 3*interval overflows. s*1000 on an Option<u64> from the body. Plain += in Counts::add. clippy reports 32 arithmetic_side_effects hits in collector.rs. Whether this panics (debug/overflow-checks) or wraps (release) depends on the profile, which is not supplied.
candidates.impact: With overflow checks, any member poisons the lock and takes the collector down. In release, node status and totals are wrong.
candidates.suggested_fix: Bound interval_s, delta_s, path_s and the counters in validate(). Use saturating_mul and saturating_add.
candidates.disagreement: telemetry/panics#1 rated it high; #2 and #3 rated it medium.

candidates.title: Collector verifies signatures and certificates of anonymous POST /v1/report while holding the global std Mutex, before the rate limit
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows accept() runs under s.lock(). Per the reviewer, verify runs at 471-477, before the bucket at 508 (excerpt). The known limit on signature cost covers directory PUTs. Serializing all collector work behind that cost is new.
candidates.impact: A flood of 64 KiB invalid reports stalls the dashboard, metrics, the sampler and honest reports, and blocks tokio workers.
candidates.suggested_fix: Verify outside the lock, lock only for state updates, and add a concurrency limit on /v1/report.

candidates.title: Registry std Mutex held across full-state clone, JSON serialization and fsync inside async handlers; certify waits behind it
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt at 361-369 clones the state and calls save (write_private with sync_all) under the lock. certify takes the same lock at 392.
candidates.impact: Writes by account holders delay certificate issuance for all nodes and block runtime threads. The size of the effect depends on the disk.
candidates.suggested_fix: Persist through spawn_blocking or a writer task outside the lock, and avoid the full clone.

candidates.title: Record Update frames are fully verified (up to 17 signatures) per connection at 10/s; no global budget across connections
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows VerifiedRecord::verify runs before any seq or staleness rejection. The reviewer cites a 100 ms pacing per connection. Combined with the connection-fill issue, this gives ~10k verifications/s. The known limit covers directory PUT cost, not the peer update path.
candidates.impact: CPU exhaustion of a node by connected peers.
candidates.suggested_fix: Reject cheap stale updates first (parse the seq before verifying). Add a global verification budget and close connections that repeatedly send stale updates.

candidates.title: Membership expiry sweep shares a select loop with the unbounded certify await; app streams and connection reuse never re-check membership
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows the sweep and the sleep_until(due) renewal branch in one select. If the certify await (beyond the excerpt) has no timeout, the sweep stalls. handle_app_stream checks only peer.contains.
candidates.impact: Peers with expired certificates keep their connections and streams while the registry hangs.
candidates.suggested_fix: Run the sweep in its own task or time out the certify call. Add check_member when streams are accepted or opened.

candidates.title: Application stream header tasks are bounded per connection only (256), not globally
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows an unconditional spawn per accepted stream. The total is bounded by the connection cap times 256 streams times the 10 s header timeout, so it is bounded but large. That makes it partly a 'connection cap already bounds it' case.
candidates.impact: Up to ~262k pending tasks and their stream state under the connection-fill attack.
candidates.suggested_fix: Add a global semaphore on pending header reads with a short deadline.

candidates.title: Collector history query aggregates all retained minutes under the global mutex
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows history() is called with c held and the range clamped only to retention. The cost grows with link growth (see the link-history candidate). Reachability depends on proxy protection of the GET routes.
candidates.impact: Repeated 7-day queries stall report handling and sampling.
candidates.suggested_fix: Copy the samples out of the lock or precompute tiers. Limit concurrent history queries.

candidates.title: Registry node registrations are unbounded per account and in total; every mutation rewrites the whole state
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt at 494-500 inserts with no cap. mutate clones the state and saves it in full. The known limit covers claiming unowned IDs, not the volume of claims.
candidates.impact: One account token holder can degrade the registry and fill its disk.
candidates.suggested_fix: Add per-account and global caps. Use incremental persistence.

candidates.title: Identity signatures are over a bare domain-tagged SHA-256 prehash; reusable if the same key signs arbitrary 32-byte prehashes elsewhere
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows digest = SHA256(RECORD_DOMAIN||payload), signed raw. If yagna or ya-relay sign attacker-supplied 32-byte values, an attacker computes digest_of(its payload) and obtains a signature over it. No preimage attack is needed, despite the scanner's wording. This depends on code outside the repo.
candidates.impact: Binding a victim identity to an attacker endpoint.
candidates.suggested_fix: Sign an EIP-191-style or other protocol-unique prefixed message. Document that the key must never sign raw prehashes.

candidates.title: Remote registry/collector error text with control characters reaches the operator terminal and logs (error_text does not strip controls)
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt at 471-485 takes the first line and 200 chars without filtering. telemetry/mod.rs:705 only truncates. This answers telemetry/leaks#4's open question: error_text does not filter.
candidates.impact: Escape sequences or forged lines from a hostile or MITM server reach the terminal or log.
candidates.suggested_fix: Escape C0 and C1 controls in error_text and in the CLI list output.

candidates.title: Peer-supplied echo replies and refusal or error text printed raw in human-mode CLI output
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows println! of String::from_utf8_lossy(&reply) and of {e:#} without escaping.
candidates.impact: A malicious peer can inject terminal escape sequences or forged lines into the operator's terminal.
candidates.suggested_fix: Escape control chars at the source with a shared helper.

candidates.title: Registry state tmp file keeps pre-existing mode (and follows symlinks); signing key may be written to a readable file
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows a fixed path.with_extension("tmp"), opened with create+truncate and mode(0o600). The mode applies only on create, and there is no O_NOFOLLOW. It needs local write access to the state directory.
candidates.impact: Local disclosure of the certificate signing key.
candidates.suggested_fix: Use create_new with a random name (tempfile), fchmod 0600, then rename and fsync the directory.
candidates.disagreement: The three sources differ on confidence (low, medium, low). Only closed-network/crypto#1 mentions symlinks.

candidates.title: Loopback and private/LAN/VPN addresses are published into signed records sent to peers and directories
candidates.reasoning: addrs.rs filters only host-internal and excluded interfaces. The reviewer cites a test at line 452 that expects 127.0.0.1 in published. Verification deliberately accepts any address (publishing policy). The loopback inclusion is demonstrated. LAN and VPN publication is a design choice.
candidates.impact: Internal addressing is disclosed to peers and directory readers, and loopback takes up address slots.
candidates.suggested_fix: Drop loopback and unspecified addresses in select. Make private-address publishing opt-in.
candidates.disagreement: records/leaks#1 rated it medium and claimed nothing filters bridge addresses. handshake/leaks#2 notes that the addrs policy already removes container bridges; that is consistent with addrs.rs:193.

candidates.title: Telemetry verify derives the expected endpoint from the certificate itself, so check_cert's endpoint binding is a no-op
candidates.reasoning: Excerpt lines 111-113 build the endpoint from cert.payload().endpoint_id and pass it to check_cert. Signer coverage is still enforced at line 114.
candidates.impact: Reports are not bound to the node's endpoint. A covered identity key is still required.
candidates.suggested_fix: Pass an independently known endpoint, or document the intent.

candidates.title: Connection cap checked on a snapshot before the handshake; concurrent handshakes can overshoot max_connections by up to ~127
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows len() read at 1095 and compared at 1100, with register happening after awaits. The overshoot is bounded by the 128 permits.
candidates.impact: Bounded excess connections.
candidates.suggested_fix: Reserve a slot with a max_connections semaphore, or re-check in register.

candidates.title: listen download releases the transfer permit before the 10 s send.stopped() wait
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows drop(permit) at 393, before stopped() at 399. Buffered streams then escape max_transfers. Memory is bounded by flow control and the connection cap.
candidates.impact: Concurrent buffered downloads exceed the configured limit on the test server.
candidates.suggested_fix: Hold the permit through the stopped() wait.

candidates.title: listen download request read uses a fresh REQUEST_TIME instead of the shared deadline
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows timeout(REQUEST_TIME, ...) at 145, while the echo path uses timeout_at(deadline) at 156.
candidates.impact: Per-stream hold time doubles to about 20 s.
candidates.suggested_fix: Use timeout_at(deadline, ...).

candidates.title: Echo reply up to ~3x request size through from_utf8_lossy expansion
candidates.reasoning: Each invalid byte becomes the 3-byte U+FFFD. Unbounded concurrent echo is a known limit; the 3x reply amplification is the only new part.
candidates.impact: Small bounded amplification on the test server.
candidates.suggested_fix: Echo raw bytes.

candidates.title: Directory pruner task leaks when the serve_with_policy future is dropped
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows abort only after axum::serve returns. It is a local lifecycle issue.
candidates.impact: Accumulated tasks and a retained store in processes that restart the directory.
candidates.suggested_fix: Use an abort-on-drop guard or select!.

candidates.title: request_timeout of a huge Duration panics on Instant overflow
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows Instant::now() + t unchecked. It is local configuration only.
candidates.impact: Local panic.
candidates.suggested_fix: checked_add, or clamp in the Builder.

candidates.title: Probe deadlines (now + duration, end + timeout) panic on huge operator-supplied durations
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt confirms the unchecked addition. The input is local CLI arguments.
candidates.impact: The CLI panics instead of returning an argument error.
candidates.suggested_fix: Bound durations in parse::duration.

candidates.title: seq = (prev_seq + 1) unchecked; min_seq near u64::MAX panics in debug or wraps
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt confirms it. The input is local min_seq.
candidates.impact: Startup panic, or loss of sequence monotonicity.
candidates.suggested_fix: saturating_add.

candidates.title: Registry certify computes now + cert_lifetime_s unchecked under the lock; lifetime is not validated on load
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows a plain +. Per the excerpt at 167-169, load() checks only key(). It requires write access to the 0600 state file.
candidates.impact: A poisoned registry lock is a permanent outage (local misconfiguration).
candidates.suggested_fix: Validate bounds on load and use checked_add.

candidates.title: CLI 'registry account add' creates the account before writing the token file
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows an exists() check, then the POST, then write_secret.
candidates.impact: A local write failure loses the only copy of the token and the account name stays taken.
candidates.suggested_fix: Create the file with create_new before the remote call.

candidates.title: URLs with userinfo (directory base, telemetry URL) written unredacted to errors, logs and JSON events
candidates.reasoning: Both excerpts format the full Url. It requires the operator to configure credentials in the URL.
candidates.impact: Credentials appear in logs and events.
candidates.suggested_fix: Reject userinfo, or redact it with a shared helper.

candidates.title: Collector rate limit keyed per signing identity; a multi-identity certificate gets several buckets
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows the bucket comes from self.nodes.get(&id) for the signer id. It is member-only.
candidates.impact: Up to 16x report rate, and members can fill MAX_NODES.
candidates.suggested_fix: Key the bucket by certificate endpoint.

candidates.title: Harness passes the full os.environ (including ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) to every tool subprocess, including cargo build scripts
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt confirms dict(os.environ, ...). Build scripts already run with the operator's privileges, so this mainly widens exposure.
candidates.impact: A malicious dependency build.rs can read the API key.
candidates.suggested_fix: Use an allowlisted environment.
candidates.disagreement: harness-python/leaks#1 rated it medium. It is low here because it is operator tooling, not remote.

candidates.title: Recovery id accepted as 0/1 or 27/28, so one record has two byte encodings
candidates.reasoning: The malleability is shown in the excerpt. The claimed store-space impact is contradicted by the reviewer's own evidence: an equal-seq, different-bytes record is compared as Older, so it is refused as Stale, not stored.
candidates.impact: Byte-level dedup and caching are unreliable. There is no storage growth and no forgery.
candidates.suggested_fix: Normalize v before re-encoding, or accept only one form.

candidates.title: Registry client sends bearer tokens to http:// URLs (no scheme check)
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows bearer_auth with no scheme check. It depends on the operator choosing an http URL. The redirect leak is doubtful: reqwest strips Authorization on cross-host redirects, depending on version.
candidates.impact: Admin or account tokens are exposed to an on-path observer.
candidates.suggested_fix: Refuse non-https unless an insecure flag is given. Set redirect Policy::none().
candidates.disagreement: Both sources rated it medium, with confidence low and medium.

candidates.title: Live connections keep identity claims after the peer record's expires_at
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows only a peer.contains check. Whether expiry is meant to revoke authority on live connections is undocumented.
candidates.impact: An endpoint keeps acting for an identity after that identity stops re-signing.
candidates.suggested_fix: Sweep or check peer.expires_at on use.

candidates.title: Collector read routes (/, /v1/state, /v1/nodes, /v1/history, /metrics) have no authentication in code
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt confirms there is no auth layer. Per the docs, protection is left to the proxy, and the default listen is 127.0.0.1.
candidates.impact: Topology disclosure if the proxy misses a route.
candidates.suggested_fix: Use a token check on non-report routes, or a separate listener.
candidates.disagreement: telemetry/auth#2 rated it medium; telemetry/leaks#3 rated it low.

candidates.title: Directory serves closed-network records to anonymous GET
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt confirms there is no policy on GET. It is a design question, because records are signed public data served over plain HTTP by design.
candidates.impact: Non-members can enumerate member records by ID.
candidates.suggested_fix: Document that reads are public, or gate them.

candidates.title: Directory checks membership only on PUT; records remain resolvable after the certificate expires
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt confirms the check is PUT-only. Members re-check certificates before storing (known limit), so the main effect is stale serving.
candidates.impact: Removed members stay resolvable until the record expires (up to 24 h).
candidates.suggested_fix: Cap record retention at certificate expiry.

candidates.title: Directory and registry servers run axum::serve with no header/read timeouts or connection cap
candidates.reasoning: The excerpts show bare axum::serve. The known limit puts rate limits in the proxy, and hyper defaults are unknown.
candidates.impact: Slowloris-style descriptor exhaustion if there is no proxy.
candidates.suggested_fix: Add timeout and concurrency layers, or document that the proxy must provide them.
candidates.disagreement: records/dos#1 rated it medium; closed-network/dos#4 rated it low.

candidates.title: Collector replay state (last_ts_ms) persisted only per minute and at shutdown
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows save_nodes in push_minute. Replay at line 505 relies on last_ts_ms.
candidates.impact: After a crash, recent captured reports are accepted again (counter inflation).
candidates.suggested_fix: Persist on accept, or add a margin after restart.

candidates.title: Collector store files and temp files written with default permissions
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows std::fs::write with no mode. It depends on the umask and on whether the host is shared.
candidates.impact: Local topology disclosure.
candidates.suggested_fix: 0700 directory and 0600 files.

candidates.title: Blocking nodes.json and fine.jsonl writes run inside tick() under the collector mutex
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows save_nodes inside push_minute, which is called under the lock from tick_loop.
candidates.impact: Latency spikes each minute with many nodes.
candidates.suggested_fix: Snapshot under the lock and write via spawn_blocking.

candidates.title: Telemetry digest has no network binding; a dual-member's report can be replayed to another network's collector
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt confirms the digest is DOMAIN||body only. It needs the identity to be a member of two networks, plus timestamp conditions.
candidates.impact: Replay of genuine reports across networks.
candidates.suggested_fix: Hash the network name into the digest.

candidates.title: download() with max_time None has no deadline and reads past the announced size
candidates.reasoning: The excerpt shows an optional deadline. Whether any caller passes None is not shown.
candidates.impact: A malicious listener can hang a client run.
candidates.suggested_fix: Stop at the announced byte count and require a timeout.

candidates.title: Out::write holds a std mutex across a blocking stdout write from async tasks
candidates.reasoning: Confirmed in the excerpt. It requires a stalled local stdout consumer.
candidates.impact: Runtime workers stall.
candidates.suggested_fix: Use a dedicated writer thread with a bounded channel.

candidates.title: Bench echo reply buffered without a size check before ends_with
candidates.reasoning: It depends on whether Endpoint::request caps reply size, which is not shown.
candidates.impact: A malicious listener could cause large client memory use.
candidates.suggested_fix: Confirm or add a reply cap.

candidates.title: accept_loop spawns a task per Incoming before trying the handshake permit
candidates.reasoning: Confirmed in the excerpt. The refuse path is cheap, and iroh's accept queue bound is unknown.
candidates.impact: Minor scheduling cost under a flood.
candidates.suggested_fix: Take the permit before spawning.

candidates.title: Peer-controlled QUIC close reason passed through as a String in Event::Disconnected
candidates.reasoning: Confirmed in the excerpt. The risk depends on consumers logging the reason unescaped.
candidates.impact: Possible log injection in applications.
candidates.suggested_fix: Document the field as untrusted, or sanitize it.

candidates.title: Registry /v1/certify does record verification for anonymous requests without a rate limit
candidates.reasoning: This restates the known per-PUT signature cost and proxy rate limits. New: the registry docs do not say the proxy must rate-limit certify, and certify also signs a new certificate under the state lock.
candidates.impact: CPU use proportional to anonymous request rate.
candidates.suggested_fix: Document that the proxy must rate-limit /v1/certify, or add a concurrency limit.

candidates.title: Record signatures carry no network identifier
candidates.reasoning: Network scoping comes only from the membership certificate. The certificate binds the network name (closed-network/crypto summary), and stripping it is a known limit. Nothing new.
candidates.impact: Same as the known certificate-stripping limit.
candidates.suggested_fix: Optionally add a network id to the domain tag in a future record version.
